title: Consent for Dental Treatment Under Standing Sedation
body:
Sample Equine Clinic. This is a fictional sample form for demonstration only.

## The procedure
Your horse will be examined and treated in the stocks while sedated but standing. Treatment may include rasping sharp enamel points, correcting hooks or ramps, and removing loose teeth or caps. A mouth speculum is used throughout so the vet can see and work safely.

## Sedation and its risks
Sedation is given by injection into the jugular vein. Most horses tolerate it well. Possible side effects include sweating, wobbliness, a temporary drop in heart rate, swelling at the injection site, and, rarely, an allergic reaction. Horses can stumble or lie down unexpectedly while sedated. Very rarely, sedation can contribute to colic or a fall that causes injury.

## Your responsibilities
Please tell us about any illness, recent medication, pregnancy, or previous reactions to sedation. Do not feed your horse for at least one hour after treatment, until it is fully awake and swallowing normally. Keep the horse in a safe stable while the sedation wears off, and call us if you notice bleeding, swelling of the face, or reluctance to eat.

## Consent
By signing, I confirm that I own or am authorised to act for this horse, that I have read or listened to this form, and that I agree to the treatment and sedation described.
